tagline: One feedback board, on your own domain, with voting and a roadmap and nothing else.
verdictSummary: Nolt is the smallest product in this category, which makes it the most tempting to rebuild and the easiest to underestimate. The board is an afternoon. The operational half — a public URL on your domain with a certificate, spam that arrives within days of launch, and single sign-on so votes come from real users — is what turns it into a weekend and keeps it from being a yes.
coreLoopDIY: Run one board on your own subdomain where users post ideas, vote once each, and watch statuses change, with moderation you actually enforce.
whatYouLose: single sign-on so votes are tied to real accounts
spam and abuse handling on a public board
the Slack, Discord, GitHub and Trello integrations
private boards for a specific customer segment
a hosted board that stays up without you
whyPeopleStillPay: Because a feedback board is a public surface with your name on it. When it is defaced or full of spam, that is visible to customers, and $29 is a small price for that being somebody else's pager.
prompt:
Build a single public feedback board and take moderation seriously from the start.

The board: post a title and description, one vote per person per post, comments, and five statuses with a public roadmap view derived from them. Server-rendered pages so every post has a real URL that search engines and support agents can link to.

Identity is the decision that shapes everything else. Pick one and enforce it: either email confirmation before a post or vote counts, or a signed token passed from your own application for logged-in users. Anonymous voting on a public board produces numbers that mean nothing, and building the board first and identity later means throwing away the vote data.

Build the moderation queue before launch, not after: hold every first post from a given email or IP for review, rate-limit posting to a few per hour per source, and give yourself a one-click ban that also hides everything that source ever posted. A public board attracts spam within days, and retrofitting moderation while it is being flooded is miserable.

Email voters when a status changes, batched per person, always with an unsubscribe link.

Run it on your own subdomain with automatic certificates through Caddy, and set up the roadmap as the default landing view — the roadmap is the reason people come back, the board is the reason they come once.

Out of scope: multiple boards, private boards, integrations, and any AI feature. Keep the schema small enough that a year of posts fits comfortably in SQLite.

faq.q: Can I import my Nolt board?
faq.a: Nolt exports posts and votes, so the content moves. Voter identities do not travel in a usable form, so historic vote counts arrive as numbers rather than as people you can notify later.

faq.q: How bad is the spam really?
faq.a: Bad enough that it is in the prompt. A public form with no barrier attracts automated posting within days of being indexed, which is why email confirmation and a review queue are treated as launch requirements rather than polish.

faq.q: What does it cost to run?
faq.a: A small VPS at $5 a month, a domain, and transactional email that is free at this scale. SQLite means no database bill.

faq.q: What is the one thing that does not survive the rebuild?
faq.a: Not being on call for it. A feedback board is customer-facing, so when it is down or defaced it is your reputation, and Nolt's price is largely for that not being your problem.
